sentences.text: Icadyptes was an extinct genus of giant penguins that lived in the Late Eocene tropics of South America, possessing an exceptionally long, spear-like beak that resembled that of a heron.
The estimated standing height of Icadyptes is 1.5 meters, and the species Icadyptes salasi stood about 150 cm tall.
Because Icadyptes salasi lived in warm Peru, penguins must have adapted to warm climates approximately 30 million years earlier than previously thought.
Fossils of Icadyptes salasi and Perudyptes devriesi were discovered in 2005 by a team of Peruvian paleontologists in the desert coasts of the Ica region in southern Peru.
The fossil range of Icadyptes spans the Late Eocene, specifically the Divisaderan to Tinguirirican stages, and it lived between 37.71 and 33.9 million years ago during the Priabonian stage.

It is debated whether penguins evolved near the poles and migrated to the equator only 10 million years ago, as the discovery of Icadyptes suggests an earlier adaptation to warm climates where today only a few penguin species, such as the African and Galapagos penguins, prefer such environments.
